body.p: A mouse-human was going, he found food, excrements of a dog. He put the dog's excrements into his knapsack. He overnighted. He put the dog's excrements, which he had found, into his knapsack and went off.[DCh]: Not sure whether "-mun" really POSS.1PL at first word.He found a small boat. Then he was going, going, going and found an oar. He put his boat into the river, he thought to sail. He sailed off, he was sailing and sailing. There the human saw a fire, saw smoke. The Chineko [lit. bat(?)] human is sitting. He is about to land [towards] Chineko (?). He landed, the mouse landed. He is about to land [towards] Chineko (?).[DCh]: The verb form and the clause appears to be incomplete. He landed, he went out of his boat, he went to Chineko. He came there, he asked: "What are you eating?" "I am eating guts!" "Give me from your gut!" "You, what are you offering?" "It will be just fat! It could be offered! Chineko, in the boat I have meat flour." Chineko went for the [DCh]: The syntax is quite unclear.meat flour. The mouse says: "Is it excrements of a dog?" The mouse slipped unter a snag, it was ashamed. When Chineko said: "There is no meat flour, there is no!" Chineko came again. Chineko came back to his tent. "Chineko, let's have a bath!" Chineko says: "We'll sink! We'll cut our hands! When holding fast on the grass, we'll cut [ourselves]!" Chineko says: "I don't want!" The mouse says: "We'll hold fast onto the grass!" The mouse says: "Let's have a bath!" Chineko says: "The mittens get wet!" The mouse says: "I'll dry [them]!" Chineko says: "They break!" "If they break, we'll darn [them] with a needle!" "The needle will blunt?" The human Chineko says: "Where is a file?" The mouse says: "In the bast basket." "Where is the bast basket?" "In the storage! The bast basket is in the granary!" "Where is the granary?" "The fire has eaten [it]!" "Where is the fire?" "Rainy wind has blown [it] out!" "Where is the rainy wind?" "When it is going there's lightning (?). I'll go to work, I'll find meat flour, I go off, I'll find my little boat, I go off. I'll find an oar."
